user_policy: Previously authorized local names and own remarks remain visible offline and beyond presentation leases. Explicit context denial, global hidden/deleted profile or sign-out removes the relevant facts.
cause: Rows only rendered names while a per-page presentation lease was live.
Page visibility, reactivation and avatar work controlled the lifetime of textual identity.
Persisted profile projections existed but were not used by centralized first-paint rendering.
implementation: Account-scoped SQLite display facts restored before publishing signed-in UI.
Shared immutable display snapshot used by names, handles, identity callbacks and avatar initials.
Public names and own contact remarks shared across contact/direct screens; group nicknames confined to their exact room.
Durable explicit denial and monotonic basic identity/remark versions prevent stale fallback across screens.
Protected-data unavailability and runtime reconstruction preserve disk facts; sign-out clears them and fences legacy reimport.
Avatar/resource capabilities and protected-byte access retain the existing authorization lifecycle.

scenarios: Expired lease, offline repository restart and cross-page reuse
No nickname/remark leakage across room contexts
Persistent context denial, global invalidation and late stale HTTP rejection
One-time legacy import and logout import fence
First appearance and reentry do not clear cached identity
Avatar decode blocked while local name is already visible
Rename replaces visible name without an intermediate nil identity
Offline startup and authentication state observation

limits: An identity never previously cached still requires its first authorized lookup.
Avatar pixels retain separate permission and cache behavior.
Physical-device first-frame timing and visual regression have not been measured.
This record covers profile display only, not full resource-center semantic acceptance.
